title_pattern.notes: Title is identical to the channel's outlier, so the title cannot explain the 14x view gap - the difference is in the hook/premise and cover frame. The real title is the first burned-in caption: 'Someone died! There's a dead body on the train!'

thumbnail.composition: Auto cover = frame 0. Black 9:16 frame; landscape band in the middle; two-line white italic caption above the band. Inside: an old man stick figure with one arm raised in alarm, a sweating passenger with red anger/shock zigzag marks, and a cropped third head at right, against grey-green train doors.
thumbnail.text: 'Someone died! There's a dead body on the train!' - white italic sans (Arial-italic look), centred, no stroke/box
thumbnail.colours: Desaturated grey-green train interior, grey stick bodies, white heads with blurred dark eye patches; only accent is a small red shock mark. Surround pure black.
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: Three mid-size characters crowd the frame; no single focal subject, no threat visible, no dead body shown
thumbnail.why_it_works: Weakly. It states a clear premise (body on a train) but shows only alarmed bystanders - no monster, weapon or body; compare the outlier's cover (silhouette + raised knife in a vanishing-point corridor). Busy, low-contrast, no visual threat = weaker feed stop.

hook.verbatim_0_to_5s: Someone died! There's a dead body on the train! I was heading home on an old-school train with my uncle when chaos suddenly broke out in our car. We leaned in to take a look, and there was a guy in
hook.verbatim_5_to_13s: the bathroom, cut clean in half. My uncle grabbed me and pulled me back to our seats, his face completely drained of color. I was about to say something, but he signaled for me to stay quiet. A few minutes later, the train jolted and was forced to a stop in the middle of nowhere.
hook.device: Shouted in-world line as cold open ('Someone died!') + first-person setup + gore reveal ('cut clean in half') at ~6 s; then a wise-elder figure (uncle) who knows more than he says, and a stalled train (trapped location) at 12 s. Then rules: 'human facial features never change', 'don't use your phone'.
hook.weakness_vs_outlier: Premise is generic (murder on a train) with no unique uncanny rule in the first sentence; the outlier opens with a weird rule ('a song plays when they strike'). Then 0:22-1:08 is a long expository stretch (uncle lore + narrator's ecology monologue about newborn creatures) with no new event - first new body only at ~1:48.

beats.summary: 'Someone died!' On a train with my uncle; a man in the bathroom cut clean in half.
Uncle pulls narrator back, pale, signals silence; train jolts to a stop in the middle of nowhere.
Uncle: something is on the train; human facial features never change; don't use your phone - it tracks you and gets you killed faster.

Narrator asks what it is; uncle: it looks human but has no emotions, an 'alternate'; avoid anyone whose features shift; 'it was just born'. Monster flashes on screen (grinning figure, gaping red mouth).
Narrator reasons from nature videos: a newborn creature outside the food chain attacks indiscriminately to test itself, disguises itself; only humans on this train.
What can track a phone signal? Not weasels/spirits/bears; horror stories are bloody, but this cut was mirror-smooth, cleaner than a paper cutter.
A passenger complains there's no signal and tries to call police; another says train police are aboard; uncle goes grim.
They flee several cars into a crowd; uncle is pale, fists clenched - the fearless man who'd sleep in a graveyard is about to lose it.
Narrator needs the toilet; uncle forbids secluded spots: 'use a water bottle, I'll block the view'. Narrator complies.
Commotion: the man who was on the phone is found in the restroom, cut clean in half - rule confirmed.
Train police cordon the restroom; passengers argue about getting off; 'relax, it's the modern age, the police will catch him'. Chatter dies down.
Narrator senses police can't handle it; wants to warn everyone but panic would cause a massacre - it only strikes in hidden places.
Passengers notice the wound; reach two conclusions (a killer wouldn't cut someone in half / wouldn't waste time) - shown with red X overlays.
'So there's only one explanation for that wound: something sliced him into...' over a giant curved blade; video ends mid-sentence.

pacing.wpm_note: Auto-captions span 0-167.9 s; ~6 words/s - the dub is clearly sped up (vs 262 wpm on the channel outlier). Captions chunk 6-14 words, 1-2 lines.
pacing.shots_estimated: ~60 distinct visual states; 46 shot groups listed
pacing.avg_shot_note: Character shots hold 2-4 s; cutaways (monster, nature b-roll, graveyard, gore) 2-6 s
pacing.re_hook_interval_s: body (5 s), stop (12 s), rules (15-22 s), monster flash (28 s), 'just born' (37 s), mirror cut (64 s), no-signal victim (70 s), 2nd body (108 s), red X deduction (158 s), blade (166 s). Gap of ~40 s (70-108) of flight/toilet with no new threat, and ~30 s of ecology exposition (38-68).
pacing.screen_time_split: ~70% character shots in carriage, ~15% gore/restroom inserts, ~15% cutaways (monster, nature photos, graveyard, train exterior, blade)

control_vs_outlier_takeaways: Same channel, same art style, same title, same voice: 26.7k vs 376k views. Differences: premise specificity (generic 'body on train' vs uncanny rule 'a song plays when they strike'), cover frame threat (bystanders vs knife silhouette), and middle density (this one stalls on exposition; outlier refreshes every 12-20 s with a new anomaly).
Ending as a mid-sentence part-1 cut may hurt completion satisfaction / shares without a series hook (no 'part 2' text).
Faster narration (~364 wpm) did not compensate; density of events beats density of words.
techniques_worth_copying: Open on a shouted in-world line ('Someone died!') before any setup - zero-second conflict
Mentor character who knows the rules but withholds the full answer ('he didn't give me an answer') - a rolling open loop
Concrete survival rules given early (don't use your phone; avoid empty places) and then paid off by a victim who breaks the rule (phone guy dies in the restroom)
Dramatic irony: show the soon-to-die passenger complaining about no signal so the viewer predicts his death
Comic-tension relief beat (water-bottle toilet) right before the second kill
Brief abstract monster flashes (glitch void, gaping mouth) instead of showing the creature in-scene - keeps it unseen
Big red X brush overlay to visualize deduction steps
Visual comparison insert (paper guillotine) to make an abstract detail ('mirror-smooth cut') concrete
avoid: Long theorizing monologue (38-68 s) with nature b-roll - no new event for ~30 s
Cover frame with no visible threat
Ending mid-sentence without an explicit 'part 2' promise
code_only_remake_needs: Letterboxed 9:16 layout: black frame, ~3:2 picture band centred (y 29-71%), italic white caption block above band, synced to VO in 6-14 word chunks

Stick-figure character rig in SVG: round white head, rounded-rect grey/blue/green body, single-stroke limbs; hair variants (messy dark for narrator, side-part for uncle); blurred dark eye-shadow band for dread; sweat drops, red shock zigzags, shake lines, blush
Expression set: worried brows, open mouth, finger-to-lips, gaping red toothed mouth for monster

Backgrounds: posterized/painterly train carriage (green seats, windows with grey rainy fields), restroom with tiled walls and toilet, black void, graveyard, train exterior - can be done as layered SVG/Canvas with a posterize + grain filter
Monster cutaway: dark void with RGB-split/chromatic glitch noise shader (Canvas), slow push-in
Overlays: brush-stroke red X slam, blood pool shapes, bisected body with red cut edge
Camera: mostly static holds with occasional slow push/pan and quick dissolves; Ken Burns for still inserts
Audio: single local TTS narrator voicing everyone (Kokoro), sped ~1.1-1.2x, low drone bed; no need for multiple voices
